page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.13xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY x86_64 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, featuring 52 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 26 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration provides 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside instruction set support including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI for vectorized workloads.

The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of memory, representing an allocation of approximately 1.85 GB per vCPU, characteristic of compute-focused ratios. It includes no local storage disks and provides no GPU accelerators, necessitating network-attached storage for persistent file systems. Network connectivity features a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps, but complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Benchmark measurements place the instance consistently within average tiers for multi-core throughput, recording a PassMark CPU score of 36,916.67 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,386.0. However, single-core benchmarks reveal limitations, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring 1,311.39 and single-threaded gzip compression achieving 22.9 GB/sec, both ranking in the weak tier. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 101.16 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 36.51 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates 40.39 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 22.62 GB/sec.

This hardware allocation delivers cost-efficient multi-threaded compute density where overall core volume outweighs per-thread latency requirements. Workloads that depend heavily on single-thread clock performance or high local I/O will face bottlenecks. The instance is suited for batch processing, web serving clusters, distributed software compilation, and parallel containerized workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.13xlarge is a compute-optimized instance delivering 52 dedicated vCPUs and 96.0 GB of RAM on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it provides 26 physical cores with hyperthreading and AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance includes 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero local storage, and no GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate average multi-core processing performance, including a PassMark CPU score of 36,916.67 and Geekbench multi-core score of 11,386.0, contrasted with weak single-core performance on stress-ng and compression workloads. With approximately 1.85 GB of memory per core, the hardware configuration offers balanced cost efficiency for multi-threaded, parallelized operations rather than single-threaded tasks. It is best applied to parallel batch computing, distributed CI/CD build environments, and containerized web serving.
